description.describe_ch: Marketing Management is one of the fundamental courses for business studies. This course introduces various Marketing concepts and their applications in business-to-consumer, business-to-business, and not-for-profit situations. You will also study how marketing works in practice and gain hands-on experience by applying these Marketing concepts in your semester project.
description.describe_eh: Marketing Management is one of the fundamental courses for business studies. This course introduces various Marketing concepts and their applications in business-to-consumer, business-to-business, and not-for-profit situations. You will also study how marketing works in practice and gain hands-on experience by applying these Marketing concepts in your semester project.

gradeRules.evalb_memo:
Absences without proof are capped to 3 times over the whole semester. Consent absences must show proof such as:
	A doctor's or hospital's note for medical conditions or a clinic visit.
	An absence approved by the university.
	An official document for attending a conference, seminar, or community service. 
For every additional undocumented absence, 2 points will be deducted from the 10 points allocated to attendance. You are responsible for tracking your own attendance and adhering to this requirement throughout the semester. There will also be attendance check during the class. The afternoon hour will be checked through the semester.
gradeRules.evalb_memo_en: For every three unexcused absences, 20% of the attendance score will be deducted. Other leave types are handled by university regulations.

gradeRuleDescribe.tpa_score_new_en:
1. Grading Components
  • Midterm Exam: 20%
  • Final Exam: 20%
  • Assignment: 10%
  • Final Oral Presentation: 15%
  • Final Written Report: 25%
  • Attendance: 10%
  1. Midterm and Final Exams (Individual Assessment)
    Both the midterm and final are in-class exams. They will be written in English, mainly multiple-choice questions.
  2. Midterm and Final Project Grouping
    The class is divided into 5 groups; each group should ideally have 5 members.
  3. Assignment (Group Assessment)
    In line with the report topic, use digital tools or AI tools to generate marketing content related to the written report. This may include advertisements, posters, videos, or other digital materials.
  4. Final Written Report (Group Assessment)
    (1) Analyze a specific marketing situation or problem of an organization and propose strategies and implementation recommendations. The marketing situation or problem is preferably real; a fictional one is acceptable if the scenario is reasonable.
    (2)Examples of “a specific marketing situation or problem of an organization” include:
    • Positioning and target market selection for a co-branded nationwide gas station credit card of Union Bank
    • Customer acquisition for ASUS
    • Enhancing the image and value of Feng Chia University
           ​​​​​​​​​​​​​​(3)Before the final presentation, each group must upload a complete marketing plan, including a PowerPoint file and a Word written report.
           (4)​​​​​​​The written report must follow the specified format and include a cover page, table of contents, and page numbers. The body of the report (excluding cover, table of contents, and appendices) must be at least 20 pages but not exceed 30 pages.
           (5)Absolutely no typos: each typo results in a 1-point deduction. Plagiarism or copying from online sources is strictly prohibited. If more than five consecutive sentences are copied verbatim within a paragraph, that component will receive a score of zero.
The Word file and PowerPoint file must be uploaded to iLearn within the specified deadline; late submissions receive a zero.

​​​​​​​       5. Final Oral Presentation (Individual Assessment)
          Each group presents based on its marketing plan during the assigned week. Speaking time is limited to 4 minutes per person; the total time per group must not exceed 22 minutes.
       6. Attendance (Individual Assessment)
           For every three unexcused absences, 20% of the attendance score will be deducted.

Participants in this course should understand that academic dishonesty undermines the educational process and violates the trust between students, faculty, and the academic community. You are expected to contribute positively to a learning environment that values ethical behavior and academic excellence.
Participants are also expected to uphold the highest standards of academic integrity. They are required to complete all assignments and projects with honesty and integrity, ensuring that all submitted work is their own. Plagiarism, cheating, and any form of academic misconduct, including fully copying ChatGPT work, will not be tolerated.
